rows.comment: Short label naming what is tracked.
Plain label listing what the mode tracks.
Accessibility label for a decrement button; direct.
Accessibility label for an increment button; direct.
Short error message that says what failed.
Button label that says the action.
Button label that says the action.
Privacy statement about the photo staying on the device; kept unchanged.
"The real map" implies the alternative is fake; say what the toggle does.
Says what is requested and the off state, but the off clause is a clipped fragment. Spell out the behavior.
lineComments: Name the download and its source.
State the off behavior in a full sentence.
rows.replacement:
'Downloads the map tiles for this route from openstreetmap.org. '
'When off, the card draws the route alone.'

rows.comment: Status message for a loading state.
"As soon as every tile is here" is loose; state the condition.
rows.replacement: 'The card draws once every tile has downloaded.'

rows.comment: Passive and wordy; "unchanged" rebuts a worry nobody raised.
lineComments: Reassurance about the rest of the card is unprompted.
rows.replacement:
'Map tiles failed to download. '
'The card shows the route alone.'

rows.comment: Privacy statement on what the private flag hides; kept unchanged.
Value with unit and time window.
Em dash and the "which is the point" flourish. State what the rating is and that it can differ from measured data.
lineComments: Drop the "feeling, not a measurement" antithesis.
Keep the one useful fact: it can differ.
rows.replacement:
'Your own rating of the effort. '
'It can differ from the heart rate figures above.'

rows.comment: Gives the two causes of a missing route.
Action label with a proper noun.
Names the source of steps and its limit.
Explains the mechanism but not the fix. Tell the reader what to set.
lineComments: Mechanism is more than the reader needs.
rows.replacement:
'No calories for this session. Calories from heart rate need both '
'your maximum and resting heart rates. '
'Set the missing one to get an estimate.'

rows.comment: Em dash and the contrast clause about strain. Keep the 0–21 scale fact and the fix.
lineComments: "effort that was measured, on its own scale" is passive and cute.
rows.replacement:
'No calories for this session. Calories from heart rate need both '
'your maximum and resting heart rates. '
'Set the missing one to get an estimate. '
'Strain above uses a 0–21 scale.'

rows.comment: Colon-joined clause and undefined MET. Define it and say why no MET applies.
lineComments: Fine, but "your heart rate and your weight" repeats "your".
"named no activity for one to apply to" is convoluted.
rows.replacement:
'Estimated from your heart rate and weight. The session has no '
'activity type, so no MET (metabolic equivalent) '
'value applies.'

rows.comment: "None of it is in the figure" is roundabout. State that no heart rate data exists.
lineComments: Roundabout; say the session has no heart rate data.
rows.replacement:
'Estimated from $met MET and your weight. '
'This session has no heart rate data.'

rows.comment: Gives two causes of a missing route.
States how the map is drawn.
Distance with unit and the same note about pinned ends.
Wordy; the title already says nothing was logged.
lineComments: "no load and no volume to total" is padded.
rows.replacement:
'No sets were entered, so there is no load '
'or volume.'

rows.comment: The mechanism is backed by the code comment on vasoconstriction at summary.dart:1538, but "not a fault" rebuts a claim nobody made. Name the body part and state the result.
lineComments: Vague "the vessels the sensor reads through".
rows.replacement:
'Cold narrows the blood vessels in your wrist, so the sensor '
'often loses the pulse. No reading here is expected.'

rows.comment: Stacked triple and a "not a fault" rebuttal. Keep the causes, drop the antithesis.
lineComments: Three causes; fine, but phrased as a list of three for effect.
"stop the sensor seeing a pulse" is awkward.
rows.replacement:
'Heat, sweat and a strap that loosens as you warm up can each '
'stop the sensor reading a pulse. '
'No reading here is common.'
